body:
This problem also exists in Godot 4.4-Dev4

If you setup a TileSet with any Tile Size you want like 32x16, 64x32, 128x64
and you put any Texture2D into the TileSet as Source 0 and then set its Texture Region Size to any size other than the TileSet's Tile Size, it breaks.

You can even paint the tiles into the TileMapLayer node and the TileSize set in the inspector is totally ignored. 
Only the Texture Region Size value is taken into account.

I also got the ghost tile

And when running the "Current Scene", i get the 
ERROR: Condition "!tile_set.is_valid()" is true.

Found a workaround that also works in 4.2 (which has the same issue) (ref: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dclc8w6JW7Y&t=64s&ab_channel=ThinkWithGames)

You need to create the atlas with enough spare space downwards, like this (I assume one tile per filled-in row):
![imagen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/315fa185-75b5-4e3f-aa69-277ac6107295)

Then when importing and configuring everything like I said in the first comment, you get this:
![imagen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2150f584-144e-4e7a-946f-906da572e60e)

Then you only need to select the removal option for transparent tiles:
![imagen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27702b60-c30d-4e74-9695-eb7518335ee7)

Then the ghost tile is gone, you can even see the orange faint line disappear. 
![imagen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efa7b91c-e8f0-43b1-a24a-166511b06674)

Hope this helps while the bug is fixed!

For another update I was able to find whats happening in the .tres file when i click on the tile to make it "useable". As a current workaround that i think is very bad/confusing I am able to set them like this... ```gdscript atlas_source.set("0:1/0", 0) atlas_source.set("0:2/0", 0) atlas_source.set("0:3/0", 0) atlas_source.set("0:0/0", 0) ```

As for the original issue reported here:

> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1.- Create a new project, add a TileMapLayer node as the main scene.
> 2.- Add the TileSet to the node, and configure the following params:
> ![imagen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c48814a7-f421-4da8-b8c9-40851e036b6d)
> 3.- Add a single tiled texture as the tile atlas of the TileSet.
> 4.- Configure the following params for the texture:
> ![imagen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a412cf87-1e29-4339-ab84-d1828119eaae)
> 5.- Run

@mpest Seems like you skipped an important step you've done, which is:

- 3.1. Click "Yes" in the auto-create-tiles dialog:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62c4b2f1-9250-4029-809a-b502fb465b66)


If you'd click "No" then there would be no tiles created at all (and hence no tile-related erros later). But because "Yes" was clicked, it created the tiles according to the setup before modifying the `texture_region_size` in step (4). Hence it created 2 tiles of size `(32, 16)`. After changing `texture_region_size` to `(32, 32)` the bottom created tile ended outside the texture, as visible in screenshot of the TileSet editor above. Which is then detected on run (and errored out).

So currently the correct way to setup it would be to click "No" in step (3.1), then after changing `texture_region_size`:

- 4.1. Manually trigger generating tiles:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ab737cc-9e80-4323-bb0c-2ad77113cd6c)|![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6ce266d-03f5-4521-8d83-aa5ef2d54493)
-|-

So this seems to be not good UX/usability-wise, the workflow might need to be somehow improved.

---

Also after the "incorrect" setup like in here the "Remove Tiles Outside the Texture" is not instantaneously getting enabled, this should be fixed:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9353a0a7-71ae-4bb8-b678-ac149060633a)
After saving and reopening the scene it warns about such tiles, and the option is enabled:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b61f99b-cef9-411d-aeb1-66ff622d97a8)|![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6589c2e5-02cf-4668-a27b-b701ac31ef98)
-|-

@kleonc  thank you so much! that worked! I also think the documentation needs to be improved here... that ordering of `set_texture` and `create_tile` is not very intuitive... is there anywhere official I can make some kind of godot documentation update request?

> is there anywhere official I can make some kind of godot documentation update request?

@meisei4 Either:
- here (https://github.com/godotengine/godot) if it's class reference related (as here are relevant files e.g. [`TileSetAtlasSource.xml`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4364ed6ccd001cbfe7cb781d074100695c878d90/doc/classes/TileSetAtlasSource.xml)),
- or in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs if it's manual related (the on-line docs not built-in into the editor (contrary to the class reference)).

But if you'd report class reference related issue in the godot-docs repo it should be fine too.
